When is a DT complex exponential e^{jωn} periodic?
column2: Only when ω/2π is a rational number p/q (in lowest terms); its period is then q samples. CT exponentials are always periodic.

column1: Why are DT frequencies ω and ω + 2π the same signal?
column2: Because n is an integer: \(e^{j(\omega+2\pi)n} = e^{j\omega n}e^{j2\pi n} = e^{j\omega n}\). Only −π to π is distinct; π (f_s/2) is the fastest DT oscillation.

column1: Average power of A cos(ω₀t + φ) and of a sum of sinusoids at different frequencies?
column2: \(A^2/2\) each; powers of different frequencies add, because the cross terms average to zero (orthogonality).

column1: δ(at) in terms of δ(t)?
column2: \(\delta(t)/\lvert a\rvert\): compressing time by a scales the impulse's area by 1/|a|.

column1: Sifting property?
column2: \(\int x(t)\delta(t - t_0)dt = x(t_0)\); also \(x(t)\delta(t - t_0) = x(t_0)\delta(t - t_0)\).

column1: Energy signal vs power signal?
column2: Energy signal: finite total energy (zero average power), e.g. a pulse. Power signal: finite nonzero average power (infinite energy), e.g. a sinusoid.

column1: Time scaling x(at) with a > 1 does what to a signal and its energy?
column2: Compresses it in time by a; its energy divides by a.

column1: Decimation by M in DT?
column2: Keep every Mth sample, y[n] = x[Mn]; it compresses time and can alias unless the signal is first low-pass filtered to π/M.

column1: Linearity test for a system?
column2: Additivity (sum in → sum out) and homogeneity (scaled in → scaled out). Zero in must give zero out.

column1: Time-invariance test, and the classic trap?
column2: Delay the input by t₀ and compare with the output delayed by t₀. Trap: substituting t − t₀ into explicit t's (y = t·x(t) is time-varying).

column1: Is y[n] = x[2n] time-invariant?
column2: No: a decimator is periodically time-varying; shifting the input by one sample does not shift the output.

column1: Tightest bound for y[n] = a y[n−1] + x[n] with |x| ≤ B?
column2: \(B/(1 - \lvert a\rvert)\) for |a| < 1, reached by the input that matches the sign of h at every lag.

column1: HD3 and IM3 of a cubic nonlinearity grow how with input amplitude?
column2: HD3 and IM3 grow as the cube of amplitude: 3 dB per dB of input (60 dB per decade), so their ratio to the fundamental rises 2 dB per dB (40 dB per decade).

column1: Why does a causal linear system need initial rest?
column2: So that zero input before t₀ gives zero output before t₀; with stored energy the response is not a linear function of the input alone (incrementally linear).

column1: Inverse of an echo y[n] = x[n] + b x[n−1] for |b| > 1?
column2: The causal inverse 1/(1 + b z⁻¹) is unstable; a stable inverse exists only noncausally (anticausal impulse response).

column1: Convolution sum and integral?
column2: \(y[n] = \sum_kx[k]h[n - k]\); \(y(t) = \int x(\tau)h(t - \tau)d\tau\). Flip h, slide, multiply, sum.

column1: Length of the convolution of sequences of lengths L₁ and L₂?
column2: \(L_1 + L_2 - 1\); supports add.

column1: Area (DC gain) property of convolution?
column2: The area (sum) of x*h is the product of the areas of x and h.

column1: BIBO stability in terms of h?
column2: Stable iff \(\sum\lvert h[n]\rvert < \infty\) (or \(\int\lvert h\rvert < \infty\)); the worst-case gain equals that sum.

column1: Why is the ideal low-pass filter not BIBO-stable?
column2: Its impulse response sin(Wt)/(πt) decays as 1/t, so ∫|h| diverges; a bounded input matched to its sign gives an unbounded output.

column1: Convolution vs cross-correlation?
column2: Correlation does not flip: \(r[n] = \sum x[k]h[k + n]\). CNN 'convolution' layers compute correlations; a matched filter is correlation with the template.

column1: MACs per output of an N-tap FIR?
column2: N multiply–accumulates per output sample.

column1: ADS1292R sinc³ filter as convolution?
column2: Three cascaded boxcars of N samples (N = 256 at 500 SPS); the step response settles in 3N − 2 modulator samples (3 output periods).

column1: Impulse response of a causal difference equation from its characteristic roots?
column2: \(h[n] = \sum_kA_kr_k^n\) for distinct roots; stable iff all |r_k| < 1.

column1: Resonator with poles re^{±jθ}: difference equation and h[n]?
column2: \(y[n] = 2r\cos\theta\,y[n-1] - r^2y[n-2] + x[n]\); \(h[n] = r^n\sin((n + 1)\theta)/\sin\theta\).

column1: Jump conditions for the RLC impulse response (capacitor output)?
column2: The capacitor voltage stays continuous; its derivative (current/C) jumps by ω₀² at t = 0.

column1: Direct form I vs direct form II?
column2: DF-I: separate delay lines for input and output (2N delays). DF-II: one shared delay line (N delays), obtained by swapping the FIR and recursive halves.

column1: Why are IIR filters built as biquad cascades?
column2: Roots of high-order polynomials are very sensitive to coefficient rounding; second-order sections keep each pole pair controlled by its own two coefficients.

column1: CMSIS-DSP biquad sign convention?
column2: y = b0x + b1x[n−1] + b2x[n−2] + a1y[n−1] + a2y[n−2]: its a1, a2 are the negatives of the a's in 1 + a1z⁻¹ + a2z⁻². Wrong signs can make a stable design unstable.

column1: Why are complex exponentials eigenfunctions of LTI systems?
column2: Convolving e^{st} with h gives \(H(s)e^{st}\): the output is the same exponential scaled by \(H(s) = \int h(\tau)e^{-s\tau}d\tau\).

column1: Fourier series coefficient formula?
column2: \(c_k = \frac{1}{T}\int_T x(t)e^{-jk\omega_0t}dt\), \(\omega_0 = 2\pi/T\); \(c_{-k} = c_k^*\) for real x.

column1: Harmonics of a ±1 square wave (50% duty)?
column2: Odd only, amplitudes \(4/(\pi k)\): 1.273, 0.424, 0.255, … Fundamental holds 8/π² ≈ 81% of the power; THD ≈ 48.3%.

column1: Gibbs phenomenon?
column2: Partial Fourier sums overshoot a jump by about 9% of the jump (peak 1.179 for ±1), and the overshoot does not shrink as more terms are added; it only narrows.

column1: Smoothness and harmonic decay?
column2: A jump in x gives 1/k decay; a jump in the slope gives 1/k²; each extra continuous derivative adds a power of k.

column1: Parseval for Fourier series?
column2: \(P = \sum\lvert c_k\rvert^2\): power is the sum of the harmonics' powers; RMS values add in quadrature.

column1: Half-wave symmetry implies what?
column2: x(t + T/2) = −x(t) ⇒ only odd harmonics.

column1: Why does a class-D amplifier offer 'AM avoidance' frequency settings?
column2: Its switching harmonics (multiples of f_sw) can land in the AM band; choosing f_sw so that two harmonics straddle the tuned station keeps them out of the receiver's channel.

column1: Fourier transform of e^{−at}u(t)?
column2: \(1/(a + j\omega)\) for a > 0; half power at ω = a.

column1: Transform of a rectangular pulse of width τ?
column2: \(\tau\,\operatorname{sinc}(f\tau)\): first nulls at ±1/τ; narrower pulse → wider spectrum.

column1: Modulation property?
column2: \(x(t)\cos(2\pi f_ct) \leftrightarrow \tfrac12[X(f - f_c) + X(f + f_c)]\).

column1: Convolution theorem?
column2: Convolution in time ↔ multiplication in frequency; multiplication in time ↔ convolution in frequency (÷2π in ω).

column1: Distortionless transmission requires?
column2: Constant magnitude and phase linear in frequency (constant group delay) across the signal's band: y = K x(t − t₀).

column1: Rise time vs bandwidth rule?
column2: \(t_r \approx 0.35/f_{3dB}\) (10–90%): \(\ln 9/2\pi \approx 0.350\) for a single pole, about 0.34 for a Gaussian response.

column1: Uncertainty principle (time–bandwidth)?
column2: \(\sigma_t\sigma_\omega \ge 1/2\) for RMS widths, with equality only for the Gaussian: short pulses need wide bandwidth.

column1: Energy below the −3 dB frequency of a single pole?
column2: Exactly half: \((2/\pi)\arctan 1 = 0.5\).

column1: Why is every DTFT periodic with period 2π?
column2: Because \(e^{-j(\omega+2\pi)n} = e^{-j\omega n}\) for integer n.

column1: DTFT of an L-sample boxcar?
column2: \(e^{-j\omega(L-1)/2}\sin(L\omega/2)/\sin(\omega/2)\): the Dirichlet kernel, nulls at 2πk/L, main lobe 4π/L wide.

column1: Group delay of a symmetric N-tap FIR?
column2: (N − 1)/2 samples at every frequency: exactly linear phase.

column1: Effect of truncating an ideal low-pass to more taps?
column2: The transition narrows ∝ 1/N, but the Gibbs ripple tends to about 9% rather than shrinking; a tapered window (Hamming) lowers the ripple at the cost of a wider transition.

column1: Frequency resolution of a record of duration T?
column2: About 1/T Hz with a rectangular window (about 2/T with Hamming); zero-padding interpolates but does not improve resolution.

column1: What does the DFT compute?
column2: N equally spaced samples of the DTFT of an N-sample record, \(X[k] = X(e^{j2\pi k/N})\), via the FFT in N log N operations.

column1: Multiplying taps by (−1)ⁿ does what?
column2: Shifts the response by π: turns a low-pass filter into a high-pass one with the same transition sharpness.

column1: Bilateral Laplace transform and its ROC?
column2: \(X(s) = \int x(t)e^{-st}dt\), the Fourier transform of x(t)e^{−σt}; the ROC is the vertical strip of σ where it converges absolutely.

column1: Same X(s) = 1/(s + a), two signals?
column2: \(e^{-at}u(t)\) for σ > −a and \(-e^{-at}u(-t)\) for σ < −a: the ROC decides.

column1: ROC of a right-sided, a left-sided and a two-sided signal?
column2: Right half-plane (right of the rightmost pole); left half-plane (left of the leftmost pole); a strip between two poles.

column1: Stability and causality from the ROC?
column2: Stable iff the ROC contains the jω axis; causal ⇒ right half-plane. Causal and stable proper rational H ⇔ all poles have Re < 0 (improper H(s) = s is never stable).

column1: Closed-loop system function of negative feedback?
column2: \(H = G/(1 + GK)\); its poles are the roots of 1 + GK = 0, not the poles of G.

column1: Reading a second-order pole pair −α ± jω_d?
column2: Radius ω₀ = √(α² + ω_d²); ζ = α/ω₀ = cos θ; Q = 1/(2ζ); decay e^{−αt}; ringing at ω_d; −3 dB bandwidth ≈ 2α.

column1: Geometric evaluation of |H(jω)|?
column2: |K| × product of distances from jω to the zeros ÷ product of distances to the poles; phase = zero angles − pole angles.

column1: Consequences of a right-half-plane zero?
column2: Step response starts the wrong way; extra phase lag (non-minimum phase); no stable causal inverse; limits feedback bandwidth.

column1: A SerDes CTLE in pole–zero terms?
column2: A zero below two poles: lowering g_DC slides the zero down and lowers the low-frequency gain; the high-frequency gain stays set by the poles (802.3ck reference: f_z = f_p1 = 21.25 GHz, f_p2 = 53.125 GHz).

column1: z-transform of aⁿu[n]?
column2: \(1/(1 - az^{-1})\) for |z| > |a|; \(-a^nu[-n-1]\) has the same formula for |z| < |a|.

column1: Shape of a z-transform's ROC?
column2: A ring centered on the origin, bounded by poles; right-sided → outside the outermost pole; the DTFT exists iff the unit circle is inside.

column1: Causal and stable in the z-plane?
column2: All poles strictly inside the unit circle; FIR filters (all poles at z = 0) are always stable.

column1: Biquad stability triangle?
column2: For 1 + a1z⁻¹ + a2z⁻²: |a2| < 1 and |a1| < 1 + a2. Complex poles above the parabola a1² = 4a2.

column1: Pole at radius r near the unit circle: bandwidth and ringing?
column2: −3 dB bandwidth ≈ 2(1 − r) rad/sample; time constant ≈ 1/(1 − r) samples. Narrow and slow are the same fact.

column1: Why does an IIR notch beat a 3-tap FIR notch?
column2: Poles just inside the circle next to the zeros cancel the zeros' effect away from ω₀, so the gain is ≈ 1 except within ~2(1 − r) of the notch.

column1: Bilinear transform and its warping?
column2: \(s = \frac{2}{T}\frac{1 - z^{-1}}{1 + z^{-1}}\); maps jω onto the unit circle once (no aliasing, stability kept) with \(\Omega = \frac{2}{T}\tan\frac{\omega}{2}\).

column1: Impulse invariance maps poles how?
column2: s → z = e^{sT}: radius e^{−αT}, angle ω_dT. Preserves the impulse response's shape; aliases the frequency response.

column1: Why are low-frequency high-Q poles hard in fixed point?
column2: Near z = 1, a1 = −2r cos θ changes only quadratically with θ, so the realizable pole grid is sparse there (15 fractional bits: no high-Q pole below ~42 Hz at 48 kHz).

column1: Spectrum of an ideally sampled signal?
column2: \(X_s(f) = f_s\sum_kX(f - kf_s)\): copies at every multiple of f_s.

column1: Sampling theorem?
column2: A signal band-limited to f_M is determined by samples at f_s > 2f_M (strict), and recovered by ideal low-pass (sinc) interpolation.

column1: Where does a tone at f₀ appear after sampling at f_s?
column2: At |f₀ − k f_s| ≤ f_s/2 for the nearest integer k; its phase flips if it came from a reversed zone.

column1: What sets the anti-aliasing filter requirement?
column2: Its attenuation at f_s − f_B, the first frequency that folds onto the band edge. Oversampling moves that frequency far up and relaxes the filter.

column1: Zero-order hold's effect on a DAC output?
column2: Weights the spectrum by sinc(f/f_s): −3.92 dB droop at f_s/2, images at k f_s ± f only partly attenuated, and a half-sample delay.

column1: Ideal ADC SNR and oversampling gain?
column2: 6.02N + 1.76 dB for a full-scale sine; oversampling by OSR and filtering adds 10 log10(OSR) dB (half a bit per doubling) without noise shaping.

column1: Aperture-jitter-limited SNR?
column2: \(-20\log_{10}(2\pi f_0\sigma_t)\): set by the input frequency, not the sample rate (100 fs at 70 MHz ≈ 87 dB).

column1: Band-pass sampling condition?
column2: \(2f_H/n \le f_s \le 2f_L/(n - 1)\) for integer n up to f_H/B; even n gives a spectrally inverted band.

column1: Why is a decimation filter blind near multiples of its input rate?
column2: It is a DT filter at f_MOD, so its response repeats every f_MOD; interference near k·f_MOD aliases into the band, and only the analog filter can stop it (ADS1292R).

column1: Bandwidth of DSB-SC AM?
column2: 2W: the message spectrum appears as upper and lower sidebands around f_c.

column1: Coherent demodulation with a phase error φ?
column2: Output scales by cos φ (lost at 90°); a frequency error makes the output beat.

column1: AM power efficiency?
column2: \(m^2P_x/(1 + m^2P_x)\): at most 1/3 for a tone at m = 1; the carrier carries no information.

column1: Envelope detector time-constant limits?
column2: \(1/f_c \ll RC \le \sqrt{1 - m^2}/(m\omega_m)\); above the upper limit, diagonal clipping.

column1: Image frequency in a superheterodyne receiver?
column2: \(f_{RF} + 2f_{IF}\) for a high-side LO; it must be filtered before the mixer, because after mixing it is inseparable.

column1: Butterworth vs Chebyshev vs elliptic vs Bessel?
column2: Elliptic: lowest order for a magnitude spec (zeros on jω axis), most delay variation at equal order. Chebyshev: equiripple passband. Butterworth: maximally flat. Bessel: flattest delay, gentle roll-off.

column1: Shannon capacity?
column2: \(C = B\log_2(1 + \text{SNR})\): linear in bandwidth, logarithmic in SNR (≈ 1 bit/s/Hz per 3 dB at high SNR).

column1: Why do phones need many filters?
column2: Each supported band needs its own filter; filters, duplexers and multiplexers are an estimated majority of RF front-end cost (Resonant 10-K citing Mobile Experts).
